metas.name: Shoplifters
metas.description: Captures a household that is a family and a crime at once. A poor Tokyo family who shoplift to get by take in a neglected little girl; shared croquettes and a beach day sit alongside the question of what they actually are to each other.

metas.name: La Haine
metas.description: Captures a day with nowhere for the anger to go. Black-and-white, 24 hours in a Paris banlieue after a riot: three friends, one lost police revolver, a lot of waiting and joking, under its recurring falling-man line — 'so far, so good.'

metas.name: City of God
metas.description: Captures violence as a career ladder for children. A Rio favela across two decades, narrated by a kid who wants out via a camera while his peers climb by killing.

metas.name: A Prophet
metas.description: Captures an education in power. A young illiterate man enters a French prison with nothing and learns languages, networks, violence and patience, scene by scene, until the hierarchy is his.

metas.name: Memories of Murder
metas.description: Captures investigators failing, for real. South Korea's first serial murder case, 1986: local cops who beat confessions out of people, a Seoul detective who trusts evidence, and a country equipped for neither to work.

metas.name: Uncut Gems
metas.description: Captures gambling mania as perpetual motion. A New York jeweller owes everyone and keeps placing the next bet to fix the last one; the film never lets him or you breathe for two hours.

metas.name: The Act of Killing
metas.description: Captures impunity as performance. Indonesian mass killers, never punished and locally celebrated, gleefully re-stage their killings as Hollywood genres, until one man's body reacts before his conscience does.

metas.name: Perfect Blue
metas.description: Captures fame eating a person's grip on which self is hers. A pop idol turned actress, a stalker, and a fan site narrating her life in first person — the animated form is what makes the slippage work.

metas.name: Heat
metas.description: Captures professionalism as a whole identity, on both sides of the law. A robber and a detective each incapable of a life outside the work, recognising themselves in each other over coffee.

metas.name: No Country for Old Men
metas.description: Captures an older moral world realising it no longer applies. A man finds drug money, a killer flips coins, and a sheriff narrates his own obsolescence; it goes quiet exactly where other thrillers go loud.

metas.name: Cure
metas.description: Captures emptiness spreading from person to person. A Tokyo detective investigates murders where each killer is different, calm, and cannot explain themselves — hypnotic and grey rather than jumpy.

metas.name: A Brighter Summer Day
metas.description: Captures adolescence inside a whole society holding its breath. Taipei, 1960 — exiled mainland families, street gangs, Elvis, a famous murder case — four hours that build a world rather than a plot.

metas.name: Chungking Express
metas.description: Captures city loneliness at pop speed. Hong Kong, two lovesick cops, expired pineapple cans, and a snack-bar girl breaking into a man's flat to clean it while 'California Dreamin'' loops.

metas.name: Le Samouraï
metas.description: Captures cool as ritual and solitude. A Paris hitman in a trench coat, a grey room, a bird in a cage, an alibi arranged like furniture — almost no psychology given, all behaviour.

metas.name: Thief
metas.description: Captures a craftsman trying to buy a normal life with one last job. A Chicago safecracker with a collage of his dream life in his wallet, neon and rain, tools on metal filmed like jewellery-making.

metas.name: Dog Day Afternoon
metas.description: Captures a bank robbery becoming a live street spectacle. One hot Brooklyn afternoon, Pacino working the crowd outside like a rally, and the reason for the robbery arriving piece by piece.

metas.name: The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford
metas.description: Captures celebrity worship in 1882. A famous outlaw ageing and paranoid, and a young admirer who memorised his life from dime novels and moves into his orbit — slow, golden, narrated like a history book.

metas.name: Thelma & Louise
metas.description: Captures escape becoming irreversible, and friendship becoming absolute. A weekend trip, a parking lot, a gun — then two women driving west, getting freer and more cornered in the same scenes.

metas.name: The 400 Blows
metas.description: Captures a boy being processed into a delinquent. Paris, a cramped flat, a teacher, small lies compounding into reform school — and a final run to the sea in one long take, ending on his face.

metas.name: The Night of the Hunter
metas.description: Captures childhood danger as a fairy tale. A preacher with LOVE and HATE tattooed on his knuckles hunts two children down a river for hidden money; they flee by boat through a dreamlike, animal-watched night.

metas.name: Spotlight
metas.description: Captures an investigation as a team slowly realising the size of the room they're in. Boston Globe reporters, church abuse, sealed records, survivors telling it plainly — no heroics beyond persistence.

metas.name: Zodiac
metas.description: Captures obsession with a case that will not close. San Francisco, years of codes, files, basements and false certainties; the killer fades and the men who chased him are what's left damaged.

metas.name: Sicario
metas.description: Captures an idealist being used as a legal fig leaf. An FBI agent attached to a border operation she is not briefed on, a convoy into Juárez filmed like an occupying army, rules revealed only after she has broken them.

metas.name: Close-Up
metas.description: Captures a poor film fan who wanted, briefly, to be the man whose name he borrowed. In Tehran a man impersonates a famous director to a family, is arrested, and then everyone involved re-enacts their own case, including the trial.

metas.name: Funny Games
metas.description: Captures the audience's appetite, by refusing to feed it the usual way. Two polite young men hold a family at their holiday house; violence happens off-screen or gets rewound, and the film keeps asking why you're still watching.

metas.name: Rififi
metas.description: Captures a robbery as manual labour. A Paris jewel heist whose centrepiece is roughly half an hour with no dialogue and no score — umbrellas, drills, plaster dust, men breathing — that every heist film since is quoting.

metas.name: The Killing
metas.description: Captures a perfect plan told in pieces that don't line up in time. A racetrack robbery replayed from each participant's angle, a suitcase of money, and an airport finale involving a small dog.

metas.name: Sexy Beast
metas.description: Captures menace arriving in a holiday villa. A retired gangster, happily fat and sunburned in Spain, and Ben Kingsley's Don Logan flying in to scream him back to London for one job — the terror is mostly conversational.

metas.name: Inside Man
metas.description: Captures a bank robbery as theatre with a purpose you have to wait for. Manhattan hostages dressed identically to the robbers, a detective and a fixer circling each other, and a heist whose real target isn't the money.

metas.name: Hell or High Water
metas.description: Captures two brothers robbing the bank that is taking their family's land. West Texas, foreclosed ranches and debt-relief billboards, and two ageing Rangers following them at the speed of talk — a western wearing a recession.

metas.name: Timbuktu
metas.description: Captures occupation resisted through music, football and dignity. Jihadists take a Malian town and ban singing and soccer; people comply in public, sing quietly at night, and play a match with an invisible ball.

metas.name: The Long Goodbye
metas.description: Captures a decent man out of sync with his decade. Altman's Philip Marlowe shuffles through sunlit, corrupt Los Angeles in a rumpled suit, the last person still taking loyalty seriously.

metas.name: Decision to Leave
metas.description: Captures desire conducted through surveillance. A detective falls for the widow of the man whose death he's investigating, watching her through binoculars and translation apps. Park Chan-wook's most restrained and most romantic film.

metas.name: Anatomy of a Fall
metas.description: Captures a marriage being reverse-engineered in a courtroom. A husband falls from a chalet roof; his wife's trial becomes an autopsy of their relationship, conducted through recordings, translations and a dog who may be the only witness.

metas.name: The Thin Blue Line
metas.description: Captures how 'eyewitness truth' is mostly people confidently describing things that never happened. Errol Morris reconstructs a policeman's murder through conflicting accounts and stylised re-enactments — and the film's evidence helped free the man convicted of it.

metas.name: Capturing the Friedmans
metas.description: Captures a family performing normality for a camera while everything underneath it collapses. A family accused of horrific crimes, told largely through their own compulsive home videos, which keep contradicting the legal case and each other.

metas.name: Dear Zachary: A Letter to a Son About His Father
metas.description: Captures grief and legal-system failure like nothing else here. It begins as a film for a baby about the father he'll never meet, murdered before he was born — then the case takes a turn mid-production that is almost unbearable.

metas.name: Man on Wire
metas.description: Captures pure, pointless, joyful daring — a crime with no victim and no motive except beauty. Philippe Petit's 1974 tightrope walk between the Twin Towers, told like a heist film by the crew who smuggled the rigging up.

metas.name: The Imposter
metas.description: Captures how badly people want a story to be true. A missing Texas teenager 'returns' three years later, older and with a French accent — and his family accepts him. The man himself explains exactly how he did it.

metas.name: O.J.: Made in America
metas.description: Captures a whole country's contradictions in one man's story. Nearly eight hours, and not really about a murder trial: Los Angeles, race, celebrity and policing across fifty years, with Simpson as the thread running through all of it.

metas.name: Collective
metas.description: Captures corruption being dismantled in real time, and it plays like a thriller. After a Bucharest nightclub fire, burn victims start dying of infections in Romanian hospitals — and a sports newspaper, of all things, uncovers why.

metas.name: Aileen: Life and Death of a Serial Killer
metas.description: Captures the confrontational filmmaker finding his limit: Broomfield builds a real relationship with death-row killer Aileen Wuornos, testifies in her case, and films a final interview in which she is plainly no longer competent.

metas.name: Tickled
metas.description: Captures an investigation whose subject fights back in real time: journalist David Farrier asks a cheerful question about 'competitive endurance tickling' videos and receives legal threats so disproportionate that following them becomes the film.

metas.name: Strong Island
metas.description: Captures grief conducted as cross-examination: Yance Ford investigates his brother's killing and the grand jury that declined to indict, addressing the camera directly and interrogating his own family's silence as hard as the legal system's.

metas.name: Man Bites Dog
metas.director: Rémy Belvaux, André Bonzel, Benoît Poelvoorde
metas.description: Captures the complicity problem pushed to its logical endpoint — the cluster's one fiction: a student crew follows a charming serial killer for a documentary, graduating from filming him, to holding the camera steady, to helping.

metas.name: 13th
metas.description: Captures the essay-documentary at maximum force — a thesis you can feel being assembled. DuVernay builds one chain from the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause through convict leasing, Jim Crow and the war on drugs to mass incarceration.

metas.name: Inside Job
metas.description: Captures elite impunity as a tone of voice. The 2008 financial crisis explained with unusual clarity and barely suppressed fury, including interviews where the architects keep incriminating themselves with total calm.

metas.name: Paradise Lost: The Child Murders at Robin Hood Hills
metas.description: Captures a Satanic-panic prosecution from the inside; the film itself became evidence in the decades-long fight over the case. Three Arkansas teenagers convicted of murder largely for liking Metallica and black clothes, filmed through the trial with access to every family.

metas.name: Tower
metas.description: Captures how people inside an event remember it — partial, sensory, nothing like the news summary. The 1966 UT Austin sniper massacre retold in rotoscoped animation from survivors' memories, switching to real footage only at the end.

metas.name: Time of the Gypsies
metas.description: Captures folk storytelling surviving, barely, inside modern crime. A Romani teenager with telekinetic powers is lured into a smuggling life in Italy, half narrated by Goran Bregović's score — Petrović's world taken into magical realism.

metas.name: Black God, White Devil
metas.description: Captures a peasant world where religion and violence are the only available languages. Rocha's Brazilian sertão — a hired killer, a self-proclaimed saint gathering followers, a blind bandit-prophet — is filmed like a folk ballad being sung at gunpoint, in glare and dust.

metas.name: The Tribe
metas.description: Captures a complete social world you must learn to read bodily or not at all. At a Ukrainian boarding school for deaf students, a student crime network runs everything — performed entirely in sign language, with no subtitles and no translation.
